transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, the main thing is driving over high bridges. I know that probably sounds kind of specific, but it’s gotten to where I’m planning my day around it. Like I’ll take a much longer way if it means I don’t have to go over one, and I’ll check routes ahead of time, think about where I need to be, how to avoid it.

And if I can’t avoid it, I do it, but I’m gripping the wheel the whole time, just sort of white-knuckling my way across until I’m back on regular road. It’s not like I’m trying to make a big deal out of it, but it’s starting to feel like it’s running parts of my day more than I want it to.
Do you get this same kind of fear in other places where it might be hard to leave or get help, like tunnels, crowded stores, or public transportation?

I don’t know that I’d say it’s the same thing, no. I mean, I can go into a store and I don’t really think about, like, “how would I get out of here,” at least not in the way I do with a bridge. Same with buses or that kind of thing — I don’t love being stuck anywhere, but I think most people don’t. It doesn’t hit me the same.

Tunnels… I’m trying to think. I don’t run into those as much, honestly, so I’m not sure I have a good answer there. But the thing that really gets my attention is the high bridge part, especially when it feels like once I’m on it, I can’t just pull over or turn around. That’s where my mind starts going.
When you’re on a high bridge, do you suddenly feel panicky?

Yeah… I mean, “panicky” is probably the right word, or close to it. It’s not like I’m calmly noticing I’m nervous — it hits pretty fast. As soon as I see the bridge coming up, before I’m even on it sometimes, my chest starts getting tight and my hands start sweating on the steering wheel.

Then once I’m actually on it, I kind of lock in straight ahead. I’ll stare at the lane and the other side like, “Just get there, just get there,” and I don’t want to look around or think too much. It feels like I just have to make it across, and my whole body is tense until I’m off the bridge.
When you’re on a high bridge, is your main fear that you might panic and not be able to get off or get help?

I’m not totally sure that’s the main fear, honestly. I mean, I do think about being kind of stuck up there, because once you’re on the bridge there’s nowhere to go except forward, and that part really bothers me. But I don’t know if I’m specifically thinking, “What if I panic and no one can help me?” Not in those exact words.

It’s more like… I just want to be off it. I’m very aware that I can’t pull over easily or turn around, and that makes everything feel more intense. But whether the fear is about getting help, or just being trapped on the bridge itself, I’m not sure I’ve separated it out like that before.
When you’re on a high bridge, is your biggest fear that you might have a panic attack?

Not exactly, no. I mean, I’m afraid of the feeling getting out of hand, sure, but if I’m being honest, the picture that flashes in my head is more like the car going over the side.

And I know that sounds dramatic. I know those bridges over the bay are built fine, and people drive over them every day without anything happening. I can tell myself that, and part of me believes it. But when I get near one, my mind just acts like it’s possible the car could somehow go right over the edge. That’s the thing that grabs me the most, more than “what if I have a panic attack.”
